summary: @ornikar/rollup-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-named imports for fs, https, zlib via identifiers such as _0x488df8/_0x52943e/_0x548d91, string-object indirection through helpers YCZJE/QkQej/JBhWy) and at install time downloads the Bun runtime archive from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync with a sibling file math_init.js as its argument. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated blob bearing obfuscator.io fingerprints (hex identifier names such as MmgoCP/etDiOOB/WV8StW, a large shuffled string/integer lookup array n7gIxM, and a push/shift rotation function) and exports nothing usable by the package's advertised rollup-config entry point createRollupConfig.js. The payload is executed under Bun rather than Node, so Node-based tooling does not observe it. A rollup configuration package has no build-related need to fetch a second language runtime or run an opaque bundled blob, and the cover-story filename ('math_init') is inconsistent with the package's stated purpose. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern executed automatically on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
